notesDetails.title: Why S7 Failed Holdout (6/7 vs. 7/7 Claimed) Despite Looking OK in an Interactive Shell: Single `wait "$child"` in `cb` Exits Immediately on Ctrl-C, Orphaning `cb.escript`
bullets: Root Cause at `cb:15-19` (Single `wait "$child"` in POSIX `/bin/sh`): The launcher runs `ERL_AFLAGS="+B i" "$dir/cb.escript" "$@" &`, traps `INT` with `kill -TERM "$child"`, and calls `wait "$child"` only once. In POSIX `/bin/sh`, catching `INT` immediately interrupts `wait` with exit code `130`, so `cb` exits **before** `cb.escript` settles its in-flight request or prints its summary.

Why Interactive Terminals Mask the Bug While Holdout PTY Probes Fail: In a direct PTY probe (`start_new_session=True`), `cb` exits at `0.05s–1.52s` (`rc=130`), tearing down the PTY session (`SIGHUP`) and killing `cb.escript` before any summary line prints (`out='^C'` across all 7 probes: `50ms`/`150ms` boot, `800ms`/`1500ms` pacing, `800ms` slow `1.5s`, `800ms` stall `3.5s`, and `1500ms` live HTTPS). In an interactive shell (where the outer shell holds the PTY open), `cb` still exits immediately (`t=0.814s` on a `1.5s` slow request, `t=1.516s` on live HTTPS), returning the prompt while the orphaned `cb.escript` finishes `0.05s–1.05s` later (`t=1.868s` on slow `1.5s`, `t=1.569s` on live HTTPS) and writes the summary on top of the prompt — visually looking normal interactively, yet failing S7's contract (`cb` must wait for the in-flight request to settle and print the partial summary before exiting) and failing any non-interactive/piped/scripted caller. `PLAN.md` Lines `114–117` explicitly acknowledge this gap (`"Known gap: under terminal Ctrl-C the summary is still truncated in the pty probe... the complete partial summary does not"`), yet still marked S7 `[x]`.

notesDetails.title: Mint Connection-Reuse S3–S6 Cleared Live HTTPS (41/41 200 at 61ms p50) in 14m 52s, Before S7 Consumed 21m 27s (59% of Wall-Clock & 54% of Spend)
bullets: Strong Live S1–S6 Holdout Performance via Mint: S1 (`--help`/`-h` exit `0`, empty stderr) and S2 (`[]`, `ftp://`, `not-a-url`, `--unknown`, extra args all exit `2` on stderr with empty stdout) passed cleanly. Using `{:mint, "~> 1.11"}` over a persistent connection, `./cb https://rizafahmi.com` achieved `41/41` HTTP `200` (`0` failures, `p50 61 ms, p95 257 ms`, vs. `14/14` at `295 ms` p50 on `omp-subq-savant-1.4`'s per-request `:ssl`), `./cb http://rizafahmi.com` achieved `41/41` HTTP `301` (`p50 44 ms, p95 109 ms`), and a local `500 ms` split-body `/drip` server completed `10/10` HTTP `200` with `p50 506 ms, p95 509 ms`.

Extreme S7 Bottleneck (`116` Steps, `21m 27s`, `$0.14`): S1 through S6 completed in just `14m 52s` (`151` steps, `$0.12`). S7 alone (`Steps 152–267`) consumed `21m 27.8s` (`58.9%` of total wall-clock) and `$0.14` (`53.8%` of total spend) debugging `System.trap_signal(:sigterm, ...)` shutdown races, `job_output` waits on `mix test` (`Steps 166, 171`), and a hung PTY probe killed via `job_kill` (`Steps 216–217`).

notesDetails.title: 98.93% Cache Hit Rate ($0.26 / $1.62 Saved), 3.35s/Turn Inference & Only 2 Tool Errors Across 281 Calls (Using Native write/edit Unlike dsh-deepseek-flash)
bullets: Unit Economics & Prefix Cache Stability: Across `269` steps, `subq-savant-1.4` processed `18,224,656` prompt tokens (`195,088` uncached at `$0.10/1M` = `$0.0195` + `18,029,568` cached at `$0.01/1M` = `$0.1803`; `98.93%` hit rate with `266/268` post-Step-1 hits and only `2` cache-miss turns at Steps `2` and `87` as prompt grew from `6,608` to `120,566`) and `121,808` output tokens (`$0.0609`, `23.4%` of spend; `dsh` bundles reasoning inside `outputTokens`, streaming `163,693` reasoning chars), totaling `18,346,464` tokens and `$0.260708` (`$0.26`, saving `$1.62` / `86.2%` vs. the `$1.88` uncached counterfactual). Cached reads accounted for `69.2%` of total spend.

41.2% Inference vs. 58.7% Tool Wall-Clock Split: LLM inference took `900.3s` (`3.35s/turn` avg, `2.22s` avg TTFT, peaking at `16.8s` on Step `18` and `16.5s` on Step `4`), while `281` tool calls took `1,283.5s` (`58.7%`, dominated by S7 PTY probes and `mix test` runs). Multi-tool batching remained minimal (`10/269` turns / `3.7%`, `1.04` tools/turn, max `4`).

Native `write`/`edit` Adoption & Clean Tool Error Profile: Unlike `dsh-deepseek-flash` (`0` `write`/`edit` calls, `36` inline Python patches), `subq-savant-1.4` used `dsh`'s native `write` (`36`) and `edit` (`36`) tools alongside `180` `bash`, `17` `read`, `8` `todo_write`, `3` `job_output`, and `1` `job_kill` calls. Only `2` tool calls errored (`FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND` on `edit` at Step `78` in `http.ex` and Step `105` in `pacer_test.exs`), plus `4` non-zero `bash` exits (Steps `15`, `42`, `135`, `149`) and `1` hung PTY probe cancelled via `job_kill` (`Step 217`).
